environmentLimitations: document.hidden === true / visibilityState 'hidden' persists throughout this automated tab regardless of focus. window.__drift3dAudioClock and window.__drift3dLifecycle (both installed inside Drift3DScene, a child of the react-three-fiber Canvas) never became readable because the Canvas's internal mount stays suspended until a frame is produced (requestAnimationFrame never fires). Worked around by reading the underlying sceneLifecycleRef (owned by Drift3DCanvas, a plain React component OUTSIDE the react-three-fiber tree) directly via React fiber traversal from a stable DOM node Drift3DCanvas itself renders — no application code was changed to enable this.

document.visibilityState could not naturally become 'visible' in this session to exercise IDLE->ACTIVE / PAUSED<->ACTIVE. Worked around via a distinctly labeled FORCED_VISIBILITY_PATH: Object.defineProperty override of document.hidden/visibilityState followed by a real document.dispatchEvent(new Event('visibilitychange')) — this triggers the real, unmodified visibilitychange listener installed by Drift3DCanvas, the same code path a genuine OS-level visibility change would take.
No .png files committed under this directory for the same reason documented in docs/DRIFT_3D_RUNTIME_BASELINE.md (save_to_disk produces an unrelated fixed desktop image).

10.1_initial_mount.result: PRE_FIX_FINDING — STRICT_MODE_PHANTOM_ROUTE_UNMOUNT — mountRevision=2 and resetRevision=1 (instead of 1 and 0) came from React 18 Strict Mode's dev-only double-invocation (mount -> cleanup -> mount on the same instance): a first real mount (mountRevision 0->1), an immediate Strict Mode cleanup that synchronously applied a full route-unmount sequence (reset with resetReason 'route-unmount', resetRevision 0->1, then reset-complete, then unmount) even though no real unmount had occurred, then a second real mount (mountRevision 1->2) starting from that fictitious UNMOUNTED state. This was originally (incorrectly) presented as a positive confirmation of Strict Mode idempotence — it was in fact the opposite bug. Historical reading preserved as-is; not deleted. Fixed via lifecycleEffectGenerationRef (the route-unmount transition is now deferred to a microtask and cancelled if the same instance's setup re-declares itself first) — see section14_correctionRound_strictModePhantomUnmount.testA for the corrected replay (mountRevision=1, resetRevision=0, lastResetReason=null after mount settles, before any real navigation).

section14_correctionRound_strictModePhan.gap: Drift3DCanvas's lifecycle effect cleanup applied the reset('route-unmount') -> reset-complete -> unmount sequence synchronously, without distinguishing a real unmount from React 18 Strict Mode's dev-only setup->cleanup->setup replay on the same instance. Consequence: resetRevision was already 1 and lastResetReason already 'route-unmount' before any real navigation ever happened.
section14_correctionRound_strictModePhan.fix: A lifecycleEffectGenerationRef is bumped on every real invocation of the effect's setup. The cleanup still immediately removes listeners and immediately cleans up owned resources/transient inputs (unchanged), but the logical route-unmount transition is deferred into a queueMicrotask that checks whether lifecycleEffectGenerationRef.current still equals the generation captured at that setup — if a new setup on the SAME instance already ran (Strict Mode), the generation changed and the transition is skipped (no-op); if no new setup ran (real unmount), the generation is unchanged and the transition applies. No setTimeout/setInterval/new requestAnimationFrame; no setState in the deferred block. The dev-probe ownership token in Drift3DScene.tsx was also stabilized: `const owner = {}` (recreated on every effect run) replaced by `devProbeOwnerRef.current` (computed once per instance via useRef), so the documentation's 'same instance = same token' claim is actually true.
section14_correctionRound_strictModePhan.method: Real Chrome session (Claude Browser pane), fresh tab, same fiber-traversal reading technique as sections 2+.
